name: Battle of Mount Gaurus
intro: Near Mount Gaurus, above Cumae in Campania, 343 BC. You are the consul Marcus Valerius Corvus, sent to defend the Campanians, who have put themselves under Rome’s protection, against the Samnites, a tough hill people. It is the first battle between Rome and Samnium.
debrief: In Livy’s account, the battle at Mount Gaurus was long and stubborn. A Roman cavalry charge failed to break the Samnites, so Valerius dismounted and led the infantry forward himself, and late in the day the Samnites gave way. They abandoned their camp in the night, and Rome won again near Suessula soon afterward. Livy’s numbers and speeches are not reliable, but the war was real and began half a century of conflict with Samnium. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: Rome’s first victory over the Samnites.

decisions.title: A call from Campania
decisions.text: The Samnites have attacked the Campanians, who have given themselves to Rome. You are Marcus Valerius Corvus, sent south with an army. The Samnites wait near Mount Gaurus, above Cumae.

hint.text: The Samnites have never fought Rome before.

scout.text: Your men have heard the Samnites are fierce hill fighters. Let them see you sure of victory.

choices.label: March straight at them and make camp close by

fx.text: You camp close to the Samnites. Your men see you confident and grow confident.

choices.label: Wait for the other consul before you engage them

fx.text: The Samnites ravage Campania while you wait.

choices.label: Raid Samnite land to draw them away

decisions.title: A hard first fight
decisions.text: The lines meet. Neither side gives ground for hours. The Samnites are as stubborn as any foe Rome has met.

hint.text: Your horse is fresh on the wing.

scout.text: A cavalry charge might break the deadlock, if the Samnite ranks are tired enough.

choices.label: Send the horse in to break the deadlock

fx.text: The horsemen charge but cannot break the dense Samnite ranks.

choices.label: Keep the line steady and rotate the front ranks

fx.text: Fresh men take the front. The Samnites have no such reserve.

choices.label: Pull back to the camp for the night and fight fresh tomorrow

decisions.title: The general on foot
decisions.text: The charge has failed. Your men look to you. The day is passing.

hint.text: Your soldiers love you: they call you Corvus, ‘the Raven’.

scout.text: Leave your horse and go to the front among the infantry. Shame the men into one more effort.

choices.label: Dismount and lead the infantry yourself

fx.text: You leap down and go to the front. ‘Show me your swords,’ you cry. The legions surge forward and the Samnites begin to give.

choices.label: Send the triarii in behind the line

fx.text: The fresh men add weight, but the Samnites hold.

choices.label: Try the cavalry once more, on the other wing

fx.text: The horse are tired and the charge fails again.

decisions.title: The Samnites give way
decisions.text: The Samnite line breaks and falls back toward its camp as darkness comes.

hint.text: Their camp is on the hillside above.

scout.text: Press them in the dark, or let them go and take the camp at dawn.

choices.label: Hold your ground; take the camp in the morning

fx.text: At dawn you find the Samnite camp abandoned, full of their baggage. They fled in the night.

choices.label: Pursue them into the hills in the dark before they can re-form

fx.text: In the dark, your men lose their way.

choices.label: Fall back to your own camp

fx.text: The Samnites rally in the night.

decisions.title: What next
decisions.text: The Samnites who escaped are gathering again near Suessula.

hint.text: They are shaken and short of food.

scout.text: Follow up quickly before they recover.

choices.label: March on and attack them again at Suessula

fx.text: You catch them again near Suessula and beat them a second time.

choices.label: Rest the army in Campania and secure the towns
Send the cavalry alone to harry them
